claims.text: Clear the full mined-block window rather than keeping partial stats when mempool reload fails
claims.quote: I still find myself thinking we should clear the whole mined-block window when the mempool does not reload.
claims.status_note: author implemented clearing all stats in push
claims.status_by_quote: I pushed both in the new push, clearing the stats and also having a warm-up time where we suspect the mempool is sparse

claims.text: Fall back to block policy on LOW_COVERAGE in combined mode
claims.quote: Should `LOW_COVERAGE` also fall back to the block-policy estimate in combined mode?
claims.status_note: author force-pushed fix to fall back on LOW_COVERAGE
claims.status_by_quote: Indeed, I force-pushed fb385bfaac...a623083db1 to fix that.

claims.text: Return FeeRateEstimationError directly rather than wrapped in util::Unexpected
claims.quote: Should return `FeeRateEstimationError` directly instead of wrapped in `util::Unexpected`? This makes the callers much clearer IMO
claims.status_note: author removed the helper function in a later simplification push

claims.text: Why does warmup end height need to be persisted across restarts?
claims.quote: Why does this need to be persisted? In what case would it make sense for a warmup to start and get interrupted and then continue?
claims.status_note: author explained, pushed a fix, and later removed the warmup logic entirely
claims.status_by_quote: Pushed a fix, warmup now re-starts whenever the tracked mined-block window is empty

claims.text: Fall back to block policy on any mempool estimator error, including while mempool is loading
claims.quote: I am slightly inclined to suggest for the sake of simplicity that whatever the error is, just fall back to block policy.
claims.status_note: author adopted the suggestion in push
claims.status_by_quote: Hmm, yeah, for simplicity, I took your suggestion.

claims.text: Should the 144-block warmup count blocks processed during IBD catch-up?
claims.quote: is the 144-block warm-up meant to count blocks processed during IBD catch-up?
claims.status_note: author addressed in push before warmup logic was completely replaced
claims.status_by_quote: Good catch, I attempted to fix it by adding a new bool to the notification that tells us whether the chainstate is current

claims.text: Could fee estimator accept stale data during IBD catch-up and slow down IBD?
claims.quote: this check may accept saved fee-estimator data that becomes stale during IBD catch-up. While it makes sense to me superficially, I haven't dug very deep. Could you check whether it's valid and should be covered in this PR?
claims.status_note: author simplified the logic in push, removing the warmup mechanism
claims.status_by_quote: So I simplify by disallowing the fee rate return flow completely; this is simpler and should handle the most important likely case of underpaying

claims.text: Should returning an error when block policy has no result be covered, or is relying on mempool alone desirable?
claims.quote: if the block-policy estimator has no result, this returns an error even when the mempool estimator can provide a fee rate. I put a small test and proposed change in https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/300. Could you check whether this PR should cover that case too?
claims.status_note: author clarified it is intentional belt-and-suspenders behavior
claims.status_by_quote: This is the desired behaviour, it's a belt-and-suspenders on `mempool_policy` fee rate estimator

claims.text: Falling back to block policy instead of returning a floored estimate when a healthy mempool has fewer txs than target percentile overestimates fees when mempool is legitimately starved
claims.quote: In the case of a node with a healthy view of the mempool, but a mempool that has less than a p50 or p75 of transactions, don't we actually want to return the floored estimate instead of falling back to the block policy estimator.
claims.status_note: author argued this is acceptable until follow-up; reviewer pushed back advocating dropping the last two commits
claims.status_by_quote: I'm not sure I agree, I think it would be better to drop the last two commits entirely from this PR

claims.text: refill the mined-block window before each cold restart test case so the assertions test dropping stats
claims.quote: test_fallback_when_mempool_estimator_not_ready deletes `fees/mempool_policy_estimator.dat` just above and nothing mines after it, so all three cases here start from an empty window, where `MempoolReloadCompleted` returns early and does nothing.
claims.status_note: author refilled the window before each test case

claims.text: use util::Expected<void, MempoolEstimationFailure> instead of std::optional for GetMempoolHealthCheck return type
claims.quote: I think this would read better if we made the return type as `util::Expected<void, MempoolEstimationFailure>`
claims.status_note: author updated health check methods to return util::Expected

claims.text: add test coverage documenting that estimator_man returns an error when block policy has no result even if the mempool estimator can provide a fee rate
claims.quote: If it's a desired behavior, consider covering it with a test to document that - please see my attempts above.

claims.text: avoid logging that mined-block stats are cleared when starting fresh with an empty vector
claims.quote: clearing `m_prev_mined_blocks` seems totally fine but the log message is a bit odd, but this is also fine as-is or addressable in a follow-up.
claims.status_note: author prevented logging when stats vector is empty

claims.text: rename the default estimatesmartfee fee_rate_estimator option from 'none' to 'auto'
claims.quote: should we rename `fee_rate_estimator=none` to `auto`, as suggested above? I agree that `none` reads as though fee estimation is disabled, whereas it selects the default combined behavior.
claims.status_note: author added a commit renaming the default estimator option to auto
claims.status_by_quote: I added a commit here to fix https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36182#issuecomment-5817784558
